title: Choose the visual world for indian-anpr
question: The roll assigned The Registration Schedule. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: The Registration Schedule
options.lineage: Indian legal schedules and notification typesetting: the rules that define every registration mark
options.thesis: The site is the rulebook of Indian plates, and the scanner applies those rules in front of you.
materials: an enamel-white plate as the only object
options.viewport: A numbered notice titled Schedule of registration marks over a real-format plate that splits live into four ruled columns (State, District, Series, Number); a stamped margin note cites the clause that fixed a misread 4 into an A; actions Read how it was built and Open the live scanner.
options.risk: Dry and bureaucratic if the motion is timid; must evoke legal typesetting without imitating any government publication (no emblem, no official heading).

raised.raise: Every reading, live or in the results, carries one fixed label anatomy: State, District, Series, Number, confidence, time.
The pipeline has named stage states (detected, cropped, read, corrected, confirmed) that each plate visibly passes through.
System states print themselves as schedule entries (model loading, camera denied, no plate in view), never spinners or toasts.
The live scanner keeps a fixed ruled frame where only the camera window and the ledger change.

options.label: Highway Signage
options.lineage: NHAI green guide signs and yellow-capped kilometre stones
options.thesis: The story is a highway: each chapter a kilometre stone, the live scanner waiting at the toll gate.
options.viewport: A full-width green guide sign reading Indian plates, read live, with distance lines as chapters (Dataset traps 2 km, Reader 4 km, Live scanner 6 km) and a toll-gate button that opens the camera.
options.risk: The most familiar Indian-road image there is; signage type sits close to generic transport-sans landing pages.

options.label: Two-ink Register
options.lineage: risograph zine covers printed in two misregistered spot inks
options.thesis: Every reading is printed in two inks that only snap into register when the plate is read right.
options.viewport: A plate printed in yellow and blue a few millimetres out of register, sliding into alignment as its text resolves; headline in the blue ink.
options.case: Holds product clarity: register is a direct picture of confidence. Loses audience identification: zine culture again, close to the fraud site.
options.risk: Echoes the hand-drawn zine already shipped; two sites by one author would look like a template.

options.label: Exposure Record Sheets
options.lineage: darkroom printer's exposure records on translucent overlays
options.thesis: The camera frame sits under translucent sheets: detection, crop and reading as stacked overlays, confidence as hatch density.
options.viewport: A plate photo under three askew sheets, each labelled with its stage and a numeric weight; sliding a sheet reveals the next stage.
options.case: Holds product clarity: overlays map one-to-one to the pipeline. Loses audience: darkroom notation is foreign to recruiters.
options.risk: Grey and technical; can read as a tool rather than a story.

options.label: Sneaker Box Wall
options.thesis: Test plates as a wall of box end labels.
options.viewport: A wall of end labels, one per test plate.
options.case: Fuses poorly: nobody connects number plates with shoe boxes.
options.kept: One fixed label anatomy on every record.

options.label: Raku Firing
options.viewport: A plate passing through kiln stages.
options.risk: Metaphor with no tie to the subject.
options.kept: Named stage states for every step of the pipeline.

options.label: Phosphor Terminal
options.thesis: The scanner as a live transcript.
options.viewport: Plate readings typed into a green transcript.
options.risk: This is the category's AI-vision cliché.
options.case: Fuses into the rut: green-on-black HUD is what every computer-vision demo ships.
options.kept: System states print themselves instead of appearing as chrome.

options.label: CD-ROM Console
options.thesis: The scanner as a bevelled console around a small video window.
options.viewport: A console framing the camera window.
options.case: Fuses poorly: nostalgia unrelated to Indian plates.
options.kept: A fixed frame where only the window changes.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A dark computer-vision landing page, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Headline and demo video side by side, a row of metric cards under it, a Try it live button.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other ANPR demo by design.
